newsitem.title: UK: Tesco supermarket sees jump in organic food sales.
newsitem.headline: Tesco supermarket sees jump in organic food sales.

text.p: The UK's leading food supermarket chain, Tesco, is predicting 400 per cent growth in sales of organic foods by the year 2000, bringing their value to 50 million stg, a company spokesman said.
The retailer has welcomed moves by the National Farmers Union (NFU) to encourage a fresh look at organic farming.
The NFU launched a publication called "Focus on organic farming," on Wednesday, with the support of the Soil Association, which sets standards for organic produce.
"Farmers and growers are being invited to take a fresh look at the opportunities offered by organic farming," NFU deputy president Tony Pexton said in a statement.
"Consumer awareness of organic farming is growing at a rapid pace and in representing all farmers and growers, the NFU is highlighting the opportunities," Pexton said.
"The demand for organic produce is now growing so rapidly that we fear existing organic suppliers may not be able to keep up with the developing market," Tesco marketing controller Peter Durose said.
"So the decision by the NFU is very timely as we need to attract more farmers to consider the organic market in the future,"he said.
Among other retail groups, Marks and Spencers currently does not sell organic produce. "We did sell it in 1989, but there was only limited demand," a spokeswoman said.
But it was now reviewing that policy. "I can't say whether we will or we won't. It's something we're looking at, she said.

Safeway, in contrast, has had organic products since 1981, a spokeswoman said. It had started with fruit and vegetables, and then moved to a wider range, including wines, dairy products and cereals. By now there were some 75 organic products on sale in its larger branches, she said.
